keyFindings.description: The lock compares the canonical sentence byte for byte, so it must stay one unwrapped 187-character line inside two skill files wrapped at about 100, and a routine re-wrap fails the lane as `found: 0` - which reads as 'the rule was removed' rather than 'the prose was reflowed'. The tester measured that exact case (test.json proof 4, the legion-retro reflow mutation). It fails loudly and in the right direction, so it is not a defect: it is the round's one fast-follow, normalising whitespace on both sides of the comparison and letting the two skills wrap the sentence like the prose around it. Named in the PR body's Fast-follow line.

The block leads with `bun test src/skills-guard.test.ts` - 10 pass, 0 fail - which is a regression lock, never a proof of a criterion. The proof is the GitHub arm immediately beneath it (scratch #2132, heads 9f9b8346 no-trailer -> four required checks success and 0af01af0 trailered -> zero check runs), and the composition run at 50f9aeaa. Nothing is missing and the gate is satisfied; a reader of the first line alone would take a unit lane for the surface. Recorded in the body's `Not proven / risk`.

adjudicatedFindings.finding: The dedupe is incomplete: `packages/daemon/internal/prompts/roles/implementer.md:49` carries the canonical sentence that `go/worker-common.md:19` already gives every composed implementer prompt; `skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md:173-175` states the fact in two adjacent sentences; `go/worker-common.md:19` keeps the `retro's removal of .legion/<issue>/` item in its `Every other push` list that `skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md:401` dropped.
adjudicatedFindings.disposition: Declined, each on its own ground. (1) roles/implementer.md is the retro worker's own role part - retro runs as the implementer - and the approved spec names it as one of the texts that must state the rule (dispatch://INFRA-149/spec, 'What this change does'); removing it would be a departure from an approved spec decided by a reviewer, which is the architect's call and not a defect in this head. The duplicate costs one sentence in one composed prompt and both copies say the same thing. (2) and (3) are restatements that agree with the canonical sentence rather than contradicting it; the defect this issue closes was texts that disagreed, and nothing here disagrees. No finding changes behaviour, hides an error or breaks a gate, so under the No-deferrals rule none is owed a fix in this pull request.

adjudicatedFindings.finding: The definition and the exception are resolved only by reading order: `a push whose commits touch only .legion/ ... ends its head's commit message with skip-checks: true` followed by `Retro's push never carries the line, whatever paths it touches`.
adjudicatedFindings.disposition: Declined. A general rule followed immediately by an unconditional exception in the same paragraph is ordinary instruction prose, and the exception is the more specific statement. Measured rather than assumed: the tester put the pre-change and post-change texts to the retro decision in six samples per arm (test.json proof 2's negative control), and the post-change arm answers from the canonical sentence.

adjudicatedFindings.finding: Minor: the PR body's first `Not proven / risk` bullet was stale - it still said no test pins the canonical sentence.
adjudicatedFindings.disposition: Accepted and fixed by me, the line's owner, before this review: the bullet now records the byte-exact matcher instead.

whyApproved: The round-1 finding is closed by evidence, not by assertion: packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts:146-174 counts the whole sentence per file in each of skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md, skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md, packages/daemon/internal/prompts/go/worker-common.md and packages/daemon/internal/prompts/roles/implementer.md, reaching the two prompt parts through this test file's own promptsRoot (line 24), never against a composed prompt, and adding nothing for the generated mirror, whose packages/claude-envoy/tests/legion-plugin-fresh.test.ts already fails on drift.

The lock discriminates: the tester mutated one text per run - reworded, reflowed onto two lines, deleted, duplicated - and every mutation turned the pi-legion lane red at 9 pass / 1 fail, the failing object naming the file with found 0 or 2 against the expected 1, the other nine tests untouched, each file restored byte for byte afterwards.

The instruction surface still states one rule: every hit of `grep -rn 'skip-checks\|trailer' skills/ packages/daemon/internal/prompts/` read in context across both rounds, with no text leaving retro's push to be decided by the paths it carries.

The new text's claims about the daemon remain true of code this change does not touch: classify/push.go:17-39 reads paths and no commit message, classify/decisions.go:59-76 records a settlement for the current head itself, api/ready.go:173-184 refuses only a Missing or red required check.
risks: READY reaching a retro head in the seconds before GitHub has created its check runs is bounded but not closed: the tester measured 26 s from this round's code commit to GitHub creating all five of its workflow runs, and the live interval between retro's push and the merger's first READY read is measured by no surface here. The architect ruled it a risk to carry rather than fix in this pull request, since the cost is one refused packet and a retry, and a wait or retry in that path is behaviour dispatch://INFRA-83 deletes. Recorded in the PR body's `Not proven / risk` for the merger to quote.
